settings.subtitle: How a box of family photos became a mission to preserve working-class American history.

settings.text: In early 2026, I found a box of old photographs in my grandmother’s attic.

Faces I’d never met stared back at me — great-uncles in work clothes, cousins at county fairs, Sunday dinners with too many people crammed around the table. Some photos had names scrawled on the back. Most didn’t.

These weren’t famous people. They were factory workers, farmers, mothers, veterans. The backbone of America that never made the history books. Working-class families who built this country with their hands and never asked for credit.
I couldn’t let them disappear. Their stories deserved more than a dusty album in an attic nobody visits.

settings.caption: The shoebox that started it all
settings.heading: IT STARTED WITH A SHOEBOX

settings.quote: These stories deserve to be seen. Not locked away in albums. Not forgotten in attics. Worn proudly, shared openly, preserved forever.
settings.citation: — The moment Tintype Thread Company was born

settings.text: Tintype Thread Company was born from a simple idea: these stories deserve to be seen. We source authentic family photographs spanning the 1920s through the 1990s — real images of real Americans living real lives.

We’ve expanded beyond our family archive to include rare vintage logos, union badges, and industrial marks from companies long forgotten. Designs from America’s manufacturing era — the textile mills, the steel plants, the local businesses that once anchored every Main Street.

Every design comes with its story documented. We believe clothing should mean something beyond fabric and thread. When you wear Tintype, you’re not just wearing a shirt — you’re carrying a piece of American history.

I grew up hearing stories about family members I never met — the uncle who worked the Pittsburgh steel mills, the grandmother who raised six kids during the Depression, the cousin who never came home from the war.
When I found that shoebox of photographs, I realized the stories were fading faster than the photos. Names were being forgotten. Faces were becoming strangers.
Tintype Thread Company is my way of making sure that doesn’t happen. Not just for my family — for all the working-class American families whose stories deserve to be remembered.

settings.title: AUTHENTICITY
settings.description: Every photo is real. Every story is documented. No stock images, no manufactured heritage, no fake nostalgia. Just genuine American history from genuine American families.

settings.title: QUALITY
settings.description: Premium fabrics, careful printing, made to last. We use USA-made cotton whenever possible and printing methods that ensure our designs survive years of wear and wash.

settings.title: PRESERVATION
settings.description: We’re building an archive of working-class American history, one design at a time. These faces and stories survived decades in shoeboxes — now they’ll survive on cotton.
